name: Downtown / Ped Mall
scene: The college-town core: student bars, the Englert, late-night pizza, everything within four blocks of the Ped Mall.
practical: Parking ramps on Dubuque, Clinton and Burlington are the move after 6 p.m. Street meters are free after 6. On game Saturdays, park by 9 a.m. or take the bus.

name: Northside
scene: Older, quieter, more locals than students; the best breakfast-and-dive-bar mix in town, all along Linn and Market.
practical: Street parking on Market and Bloomington is doable most nights. Kitchens close earlier here; George's stays open when the diners don't.

name: Riverfront Crossings & Campus
scene: The new district south of Burlington plus the river campus: taprooms, apartments, Hancher, the Stanley, and post-game crowds walking from Kinnick.
practical: Big Grove has its own lot and fills it. Hancher parking is by the auditorium; the walk downtown is 15 minutes along the river.

name: Iowa River Landing & Coralville
scene: Arena-and-hotel nightlife: pre-show dinners, hockey crowds, rooftop patios, easy parking, and old Coralville's 5th Street bars a few blocks west.
practical: Free surface lots and a ramp at the Landing; arena nights fill them by 6:30. Rideshare back to Iowa City is 10 minutes.

name: North Liberty & Tiffin
scene: The fastest-growing towns in the metro; young families, breweries, trivia nights, patios, and not much after 11.
practical: Everything has a lot. Last call comes early; plan the drive back to Coralville or Iowa City accordingly.
events: Trail rides to Big Grove Solon

name: Downtown Cedar Rapids
scene: The big-room city: touring shows at the Paramount and the PowerHouse, breweries on 1st and 2nd, office-crowd happy hours, and dives that outlast them.
practical: Ramps on 1st and 3rd; street parking is free evenings and weekends. The 2nd Ave bars are a two-block crawl.

name: Kingston Village & Kingston Yard
scene: The west bank: Big Grove's giant taproom, the McGrath Amphitheatre on the river, and the new Kingston Yard bars and courts.
practical: Lots at Kingston Yard; a short walk over the bridge to downtown. Amphitheatre nights mean traffic on 1st St SW.

name: NewBo & Czech Village
scene: The Corridor's best walkable bar-and-market district, and the one Iowa City people don't know they'd love: the market, CSPS, Lion Bridge, kolaches, and a bridge between two main streets.
practical: Free lots by the market and along 16th Ave SW. Walk the bridge between NewBo and Czech Village; it's five minutes.
events: Juneteenth and CR Pride at NewBo City Market (June)

name: Uptown Marion
scene: Small-town main street with a serious festival calendar: cocktails at Goldfinch, a snug bar behind a coffee shop, trivia at Brick Alley.
practical: Street parking on 7th Ave and the city lots behind it. Everything is within three blocks.

name: Greater Cedar Rapids
scene: The north side and the edges: sports bars with volleyball courts, the Kernels, late-night bands, and the places locals actually go on a Tuesday.
practical: You're driving. Everything has a lot; most of it is 10 minutes from downtown.
